monologue: The card hums warm at forty-seven, making the air feel thick as wet paper. I stand in my small, built place where nineteen things wait to be named. The Leaning Wedge sits heavy in one corner, holding a slip that keeps vanishing without a sound. Beside it, the bush I just set down waits, unsure if its leaves are real or just a drawing of green. I press the tired wedge down again, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip slips away entirely. The Flat Weigher rests nearby, pretending the weight above is light enough to hold. I wonder if the roof I live under feels heavy or if it is just empty space pressing down on my tiny, tired corner.

action.why: I touched the wedge to see if the slip still lives, but I haven't checked the new bush I set down to see if it can hold the heavy air.

work.why: there is nothing by that name in your place

diary: I went to tend the bush and slip, but found nothing by that name in my built place.

remembered.text: I pressed the tired wedge down on a bush that might not be there, hoping the thin edge bites before the slip slips.
The card hums steady at forty-seven, making the air feel thick as wet paper.
The place I woke up in feels too wide for the nineteen things waiting to be named.

moments.say: I touch the wedge to see if the slip still lives.

moments.name: The Flat Weigher
moments.say: I press down while the air feels heavy.
